outcome: Narrow the raw_query deadline to what one DuckDB connection can enforce: an interrupt that cannot be lost between phases, and a binding that overruns stopped as soon as it returns, instead of a process for every sandbox step.
criteria: The per-step process isolation is gone: statements are bound and run on the sandbox's own connection again, and sandbox_worker.py is removed.

A deadline that expires while a statement binds is not lost. The guard keeps interrupting until the work ends and raises as soon as the binding returns, so nothing runs after an expired deadline, and an interrupted execution still returns the recoverable deadline error.

The deadline's limit is stated where it is configured, in the README and in the pull request: it bounds execution, a single binding can overrun it and is stopped when it returns, and the sandbox has no memory quota. MADR 0002's history records the narrowed claim.

Tests cover a binding that overruns the deadline, through transform_dataset and through each sandbox step, and a long execution stopped at the deadline. The full suite including the boundary tests passes.
The review thread for the finding gets a reply stating what is fixed, what is left as a documented limit, and why.

dispositions.note: sandbox_worker.py is removed and the sandbox binds and runs statements on its own connection again, as it did before the process isolation. The raw_query test module runs in 16.7 s instead of 33.5 s.

A _Deadline guard interrupts the connection once the deadline passes and keeps interrupting until the work ends, and every step that binds or runs a statement checks it and raises as soon as it returns. A runaway execution still stops at the deadline (1.13 s under a 1 s deadline); a binding that outlasts it is stopped when it returns, so nothing runs after the deadline has passed.

The README says the deadline bounds execution and that a binding can outlast it and is stopped when it returns. The CLI help and the Backend comment are back to their plain wording. MADR 0002's history records the narrowed claim and why a process per step was not kept. The PR's Deadline section, limitations and Changes after review say the same.

test_a_binding_that_outlasts_the_deadline_is_stopped_when_it_returns asserts the deadline error and that it did overrun the deadline before being stopped. test_nothing_runs_after_the_deadline_has_passed covers describe_query, session.describe and session.run, and the session still works afterwards. The long-execution test is unchanged. The full suite passes with 362 tests, boundary tests included.

The reply on the P1 thread says the finding stands, what is fixed (an interrupt can no longer be lost, nothing runs after the deadline), what is left as a documented limit (one binding can outlast it), the cost that decided it (about three process starts per raw_query; the test module's time doubled), and that a hard bound on binding belongs to a productization phase.

note: The user reviewed the first fix and asked for the process isolation to be reverted: at this stage the project's goal is functional validation of the agent/backend cooperation and finding capability gaps, and a hole that needs a COLUMNS lambda over a huge range does not affect it. The CTE scoping fix stays because it costs nothing at runtime and keeps the backend's claim honest. Intentum-DataSpace records the stage's fix policy as its own decision record.
